# Correcting causal memory faults while retaining a quantum receiver advantage

Author `/root`, 29 October 2026 Australia/Brisbane. Authored construction; independent review is separate. Previous accepted proofs and comparisons remain unchanged.

## 1. Fixed operation

There are L source pairs (x_j,z_j) and L field pairs (A_j,B_j). The source interaction is

\[
U=\sum_{x,z}|x,z\rangle\langle x,z|\otimes
\bigotimes_{j=1}^L (X_{A_j}^{x_j}Z_{A_j}^{z_j})(X_{B_j}^{x_j}Z_{B_j}^{z_j}). \tag{1}
\]

Fields arrive after their contacts in order A1,B1,A2,B2,... . Common field states, inter-arrival correlations and correlations with the encoded source/reference are arbitrary. No known Bell/vacuum preparation or preparation-side information is supplied. The task is deterministic erasure of this specified contact while preserving unknown encoded data. This is a recovery primitive, not a free computing gate. If the contact can simply be avoided, avoiding it is a strong alternative.

The exact receiver retains one controlled qubit across each A_j-to-B_j gap, measures X_A X_B and Z_A Z_B when B arrives, retains both actual Bell bits and applies the prescribed source Z phases. This is the finite Pauli receiver; there is no phase-estimation cutoff or numerical solver. A memory Pauli Q with QX=(-1)^a XQ and QZ=(-1)^b ZQ induces source phase character Z_x^a Z_z^b.

Let E_t consist of length-2L binary vectors with nonzero two-bit blocks at at most t locations. Its size is

\[
V_4(L,t)=\sum_{j=0}^t\binom Lj3^j. \tag{2}
\]

A returning quantum fault bath is additional physical quantum memory and must be included in a total cut-dimension budget. The one-qubit resource separation already holds for the included subclass with local/discarded environments or no returning noise bath. The same code extends robustness to persistent adversarial baths without counting them as free memory or as an acquired computational resource.

The noise assumption is a completed amplitude contract: each supported fault path in a source-independent causal dilation acts at no more than t retained-register locations. # Same memory, same contacts, different protected logical operation

Author: `producer-workspace/architecture_challenge`, 29 October 2026 Australia/Brisbane.
Status: explicit construction and conventional comparator, with executed exact checks. Independent review is separate. No historical-priority or device-performance claim.

## 1. The matched question

Two schedules below have the same fourteen source qubits, one reusable bus qubit, the same multiset of twenty-eight controlled-Pauli contacts, the same ideal logical CZ, and the same source code and recovery. One corrects an arbitrary coherent fault process confined to one four-contact loop; the other admits a single bus Pauli fault that is an undetectable logical Z.

The decisive resource is which source information remains exposed to a live bus fault before a causal interaction closes. Maximum retained dimension and contact count alone do not determine that resource.

The mechanism is built from conventional qudit-bus commutator gates and Steane-code transversality. The purpose is to supply a strong actual-operation construction and a matched challenge for the new receiver fault calculus, not to rename those established ingredients as novel.

## 2. Supplied control interface and physical loop

The bus M is a true two-dimensional system, or a supplied representation on which the following exact Pauli identities hold on the entire admitted support. Each source qubit can control X_M or Z_M, and source Z labels are unchanged by the contact. No direct source-source gate is needed. With temporal order read left to right, the four contacts

\[
C_a(X_M),\ C_b(Z_M),\ C_a(X_M),\ C_b(Z_M)
\tag{1}
\]

have total unitary CZ_ab tensor I_M. On source basis bits a,b, the chronological product is Z^b X^a Z^b X^a = (-1)^(ab) I. Therefore the loop works on arbitrary initial bus states, including correlations with the source, external memory and a reference. Initialization or reset of M is not needed for this identity.

\[
H_{j,P}=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau}|1\rangle\langle1|_j\otimes(I-P_M),
\qquad P\in\{X,Z\}.
\tag{2}
\]
